segments.label: Nell
segments.text: In the Voice House, everyone was asleep, except Pip, the smallest pillow on the sofa.

segments.label: Pip
segments.text: Nell? Nell, are you awake? The lamp in the hallway is humming, and I can't stop listening to it.

segments.label: Nell
segments.text: Pip tiptoed up the stairs, past forty sleeping portraits, all the way to the attic door.

segments.label: Hoot
segments.text: Who goes there, at this hour of the night?

segments.label: Pip
segments.text: It's only me, Professor Hoot. The hallway lamp won't stop humming.

segments.label: Hoot
segments.text: Hmm. Lamps don't hum for nothing, little one. Lamps hum when they're lonely.

segments.label: Nell
segments.text: Just then, a tiny voice squeaked from inside the pantry.

segments.label: Tilly
segments.text: Lonely? I'll keep it company! I've got crumbs, and I know three songs!

segments.label: Nell
segments.text: So the three of them sat beneath the hallway lamp, and Tilly sang her first song, about cheese.

segments.label: Tilly
segments.text: Oh, cheddar in the morning, and brie before bed!

segments.label: Hoot
segments.text: That is a terrible song. Sing it again.

segments.label: Nell
segments.text: She sang it again, and the lamp hummed a little softer. Her second song was about the moon.

segments.label: Tilly
segments.text: The moon is a cracker, the moon is a cracker, nibble it slowly and the night gets darker.

segments.label: Pip
segments.text: Look! It's flickering. I think it's laughing.

segments.label: Nell
segments.text: And by her third song, the lamp's hum had turned into a gentle purr, like a cat full of milk.

segments.label: Hoot
segments.text: There. Nobody likes to be the only one awake.

segments.label: Nell
segments.text: Pip curled up on the hall rug, Hoot tucked his head under his wing, and Tilly fell asleep mid-chorus. And the lamp, glowing softly, watched over all of them until morning.
